newsitem.title: GERMANY: Ifo - E. German upturn still not self-sustaining.
newsitem.headline: Ifo - E. German upturn still not self-sustaining.

text.p: East Germany's economy has not yet achieved self-sustaining growth and the strong expansion seen in the early 1990s is over, the Ifo ecnomic research institute said on Tuesday.

Ifo predicted in its half-yearly economic outlook that east Germany' gross domestic product (GDP) would grow by 2.0 percent in 1997 and by 2.5 percent in 1998, below projected growth rates of 2.25 percent and 2.75 percent respectively for west Germany.
"Seven years after currency union (with west Germany) the period of high growth rates in the new federal states is over, the process of catching up slowed markedly in 1996," Ifo said.
"It appears that self-sustaining growth could not be triggered despite exeptionally high investment rates." Real GDP in 1996 grew by just 2.0 percent.
But the report added that sentiment in the region's manufacturing sector had improved in the second half of 1996 and that lively demand now signalled a "solid upward trend."
Industrial production is expected to rise by just under 10 percent in 1997, with the investment goods industry enjoying the strongest growth, Ifo said.
But earnings across east German industry remained "completely insufficient," Ifo said. It added that the decline in employment in the region had still not ended but had slowed.
